title: STEP import refuses a legal file: a boundary point lies off a twisted B-spline surface

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.

title: Rotary operations: state the heights as radii about the rotary axis (clearance, retract, top, bottom cylinders), not Z planes

body:
Requested by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), while setting up the helical rotor of #2772 on an A table.

## What happens

The rotary operations (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) show the same Heights page as the 3-axis operations: Clearance, Retract, Top and Bottom as Z values in the setup frame (the viewport labels them, e.g. "Clearance 3.6733 (stock top +0.9843)"). On a part that turns about A, a Z plane is the wrong shape: the tool must keep its distance from the axis all the way round. The #1904 walkthrough already notes that "Bottom Z is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius".

## Wanted

For an operation on a rotary, the heights are cylinders about the fitted (or, after #2772, stated) rotary axis:

- **Clearance radius** and **retract radius**: the tool moves between cuts at this distance from the axis while A turns;
- **Top radius** / **bottom radius** (or depth from the stock skin): the radial band the passes cut, the 4-axis equivalent of Top/Bottom;
- each one offered "from stock OD", "from model max radius" or an absolute radius, the way the Z heights offer "from stock top / model top" today;
- the viewport draws them as cylinders (or circles in the axis view), not planes.

## Safety

- Every radius is checked against the stock and the fixture (chuck, tailstock): a clearance radius inside the stock's largest radius is refused at the setting, not found at simulation.
- The A-only moves (the part turns while the tool waits) happen at the clearance radius, so they are judged by the existing swing / collision checks.
- Changes the posted G-code of rotary operations: golden tests for the old Z-height behaviour stay until the new heights are the default, and the change is noted as breaking for rotary projects if the saved fields change.

## Done means

A rotary operation shows the four heights as radii, the generated path keeps them (pinned by a test that measures the tool tip's distance from the axis on every link and rapid), the viewport draws them about the axis, and a radius inside the stock is refused by name.

Related: #2772 (stated axis for a helical part).

title: Rotary ops refuse a helical part (screw rotor) on an A table: the axis is fitted from the normals only, never taken from the machine's rotary line

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

body:
Requested by @vilts (relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), after the #2603 kit ran clean in his Robodrill's Manual Guide i graphic simulation: today the simulation draws a default blank, and he does not know how to set it by hand.

## What

Manual Guide i reads a blank (stock) definition block near the top of a program and uses it in the animation. An **opt-in** Fanuc post option writes the setup's stock as that block, after the program number and before the first motion.

Codes as the user's reading of the manual summarises them (to be verified against the manual):

| Code | Blank |
|---|---|
| G1902 | rectangular block: B width (X), D depth (Y), H height (Z), I/J/K = X/Y/Z distance from the block's lowest corner to the work origin |
| G1900 | round bar (along Z) |
| G1906 | round bar along X |
| G1901 / G1907 | hollow round bar (along Z / X) |
| G1903 / G1904 | square bar / hollow square bar |

Example (100 x 60 x 30 block, G54 at the top centre): `G1902 B100. D60. H30. I50. J30. K30.`

Source (public Fanuc documentation, behaviour only): Manual Guide i milling and turning operator's manual, https://www.cnc.uk.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Manual-Guide-Milling-and-Turning-Manual.pdf

## Rules

- **Off by default.** A control without Manual Guide i can alarm on G1902, so the option is per machine (a machine/post property, e.g. "Manual Guide i blank"), never on for every Fanuc output.
- Box stock -> G1902; a cylinder stock -> G1900 (or G1906 when its axis is X); any other stock shape -> no block and a comment saying why, not a wrong block.
- I/J/K come from the setup's WCS origin relative to the stock's minimum corner, in program units (G20/G21), with the signs the manual gives. A yawed or rotated WCS that the block cannot describe -> no block plus a comment.
- No other post output changes (golden files stay the same with the option off).

## Research first (agent)

Read the manual's blank-figure section and confirm: the exact address letters and signs for G1902 and G1900 (incl. the bar's length and the axis position), where in the program the block must stand (before or after G90/G54, before the first tool change), whether it needs Manual Guide i "animation" mode only, and inch behaviour. Record the answers here before code.

## Done means

- The Fanuc post has the option, off by default; with it on, a box stock and a cylinder stock each post the right block (golden tests), and an unsupported stock posts a comment, not a block.
- vilts confirms in his Manual Guide i simulation that the drawn blank matches the stock (one short kit file).
- Clean-room: Fanuc's public manual only; no other CAM's post or output consulted.

body:
Follow-up of PR #2717 (review 5974923122, a note that was not a blocker).

## What is wrong

`RasterGrid::cell_rect` in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster.rs` multiplies two `i64` values (`i * cell`) before the add. `RasterGrid::new` proves only that `origin + n * cell` fits in `i64`. With an origin near `i64::MIN` and a cell near `i64::MAX / n`, the intermediate product can overflow.

No current path can build such a grid: `covering` keeps the origin near the region. The code has no callers outside its tests. Thus this is owed hardening, not a defect.

## What to do

- Compute the corner in `i128` and convert to `i64` with a checked conversion.
- Refuse an overflow by name. Do not wrap and do not panic.
- Add one test with a hand-made grid at the limits.

Done means: `cell_rect` has no unchecked `i64` product, and the test pins the limit case.

body:
Found during the work on #2754.

## What we saw

The test `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (`crates/app/tests/shoulder_adaptive.rs`) asserts that the last feed move ends at the selected face (distance = tool radius).

During #2754, a trial mesh of `fig8.step` divided the boundary edges of the cone faces by 2.0 in place of 1.5. That mesh is also full fidelity (chord 0.005 mm). The changes to the part were small:

- The outline Y range went from `-29.99511 .. 166.015336` to `-30.0 .. 166.017784`.
- The outer outline loop went from 2520 to 3489 points.

With that mesh, the Adaptive2D path did not end at the wall. After the wall pass (moves 1721-1935) it retracted and cut two more rings at the stock edge (moves 1939-1956, x = +/-51.5). The last feed ended 31.406 mm from the part. The minimum distance to the part stayed 3.999-4.000 mm, so there was no gouge.

The divisor that #2754 ships (1.5) gives a path that ends at the wall, and the test passes. The trial divisor is not on any branch.

## Why it matters

The path order of Adaptive2D with Outside containment changes a lot for a small change of the mesh. A later importer change can make the test red again, or end a user's path with an air ring after the finish pass.

## Done means

- Find why a stock-edge ring can be cut after the wall pass (rest region, region split, or order rule).
- Make the wall pass the last pass, or record why the order is correct.
- A pinning test with a small perturbation of the part outline.

body: ### What are you trying to do I want to describe my own machine in the Machines pane, for example a 3-axis grblHAL mill with a 4th-axis rotary (A, about X) on the table. The file editor (machine_file_editor.rs) shows one field for each key the file already has (machine::fields). It cannot add an axis, remove one or change their order in kinematics.default.parts. Today I have to edit the .mch file in a text editor and reload it. ### How you imagine it working - One row per axis part, in chain order, under `table` or under `head` in `kinematics.default.parts`, with up, down and remove buttons and an "add axis" control. A linear part is `X`, `Y`, `Z` (and `U`, `V` for a wire machine); a rotary part is `A`, `B` or `C`. - A linear row edits `direction` (`1` / `-1`, #373). - A rotary row edits `axis` (±X, ±Y, ±Z, or three numbers for any other vector) and its travel, or none for continuous. - A rotary that turns the work also edits `nose_to_axis` and `axis_to_table` (#785), the two distances the clearance gates read. They are measurable with a rule or taken from the maker's data. - Under them, a collapsed "Kinematics" group holds `pivot` and `offset` (#1962). It is closed by default and open when the file already states a pivot. For a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head), the group is open instead, since the two distances do not apply to it and the pivot is what places it. This issue only adds the group; #1970's rows fill it (see below). - The letter follows the `axis` by RS-274: about X is `A`, about Y is `B`, about Z is `C`. When `axis` is set, the editor suggests that letter. A row whose letter and `axis` disagree (an `A` about Y, say) shows a note at the row; whether that should also block a save is the validator's call, as now. - The edits go through `MachineDraft`, as `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant` do, so keys the editor does not know are kept. - The validator judges the result as now. A refusal shows at the row it concerns, and a save stays blocked while a refusal stands. - Moving a rotary changes its `parent` and `chain_order`, since the parser derives them from the nesting (#1962). Tests pin that, and that `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` survive an add, a move and a remove. For illustration only, the axis list as it started to look in another CAM tool (solidcraft). It is a hint at the idea, not a layout to copy. Its `Pivot` row stands in the open; the proposal here puts the pivot in a collapsed group instead. **Overlap with #1970.** #1970 adds rows for the #1962 trunnion keys to `fields.rs` and `sheet.rs`, the same files and the same rotary row. This issue does not edit those keys; it only keeps them, and the rotary row's collapsed "Kinematics" group is where #1970's rows go. Its blockers (#1962, #1965, #1968) look done on `main`, so the two may run at the same time. Should this one wait for #1970, go first, or be folded into it? **A question before any code.** A rotary can be placed by `nose_to_axis` / `axis_to_table` (#785) or by `pivot` / `offset` (#1962). I do not see them as alternatives: the clearance gates read the #785 pair, the post's kinematics the #1962 pair, so a file may well want both. Hence the proposal above rather than a choice between them: a rotary that turns the work shows the two distances, with `pivot` / `offset` in a collapsed group; a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head) shows the group open, since the two distances do not apply to it. Does that split work for you, or should the editor show both pairs alike? **And one about a machine with both.** `nose_to_axis` is measured with Z at `safe_retract`, and as I read it with the head straight. On a machine with a tilting head (B under `head`) and a rotary that turns the work (A under `table`), the nose moves away from that line as B tilts, so the one number no longer holds. Do the index-swing gates handle such a machine today? If not, should the editor still offer the two distances on its A, or say that they are judged only with the head straight? I would like to take this one if it is wanted.

body:
**What happens:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (and every gate built on it: merge trains, post-merge checks) runs its ~620 steps strictly one after another (`xtask/src/exec.rs`, "the one-at-a-time loop"). Each step compiles and links one test binary, then runs it. Linking a large Rust test binary uses about one core.

**Evidence (2026-11-19, merge train on a 16-core Hetzner ccx43, main 409c0b5ab + one PR):**
- 1 h 20 min wall time; load average 2.7-2.8 on 16 cores for most of the run; the provider's CPU graph sits at ~100-300 % of 1600 %.
- At the moment checked: step 623 (`app suites: pocket3d_reach`), one `rustc` at 100 %, nothing else busy.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` was set; it scales `-j` and `--test-threads` inside a step, but the steps themselves do not overlap.

The release tier already has parallel lanes (#2057, the longest-first queue of #2461), which took the release gate from 114.6 to 52.7 min. The batch tier does not use them.

**Proposal (two parts, either helps):**
1. **One parallel prebuild:** before the steps, build every test binary the plan needs in one cargo call (`cargo test --no-run -j N` over the planned packages/targets, with the same profile and features the steps use, so the steps reuse the artifacts instead of relinking one by one).
2. **Lanes for batch:** run the batch steps through the release queue's lanes (longest first, sharing the job budget), so several test binaries run at once.

Keep what the gate guarantees today: every step still runs and is logged, a red step still fails the gate, VOID detection is unchanged.

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate batch` on a 16-core host uses most of its cores during the build phase, and its wall time drops substantially against the same commit (measure before/after on the same machine; numbers in the PR).

Related: #2461, #2057, #2556, #2557.

`ImportModel::within` (crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs, #2463) reads and parses the file, then reads the file a second time for its SHA-256. If the file changes between the two reads, the model holds the first bytes and the link records the second digest. The link check then sees no change. That change is never imported.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Link a model to a file, or import the file.
2. Change the file while the import parses it (a large model, one save during the parse).
3. The model keeps the old geometry. Its operations do not go Stale. The status line says nothing.

## Workaround

Save or touch the file once more. The digest differs from the recorded one, and the check imports the file again.

## What Should Happen

Read the file once. Take the digest from the bytes that the parse used. `ImportModel::graded` already takes bytes in hand; use the same path for a file import.

## Source

Found in the review of PR #2563 (head `aef4f610c`), 2026-11-19. The code comment in `within` names the window. The window is one parse time.

Reported by a Sodick wire EDM owner (@spikeypineapple) on #617, 2026-11-16:

> I can say for sure this won't work. It might work on older machines, but it won't run on a ln1/ln2/ln3 control (anything made in the last 20 years).

**What the LN controls expect** (his report): the condition codes follow the passes:
- `C000` - entering the cut (a stable condition, so the wire does not break)
- `C001` - rough cut
- `C002` - sizing / second cut
- `C903` and up - polishing passes

**What the post does now** (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, main 1ae4d061f):
- writes ONE condition word per operation, the operation's own condition id (`C` + three digits), line 296;
- refuses a condition change between passes (skims), line 186, and sends skims to `wire-iso` instead;
- writes no entry condition before the cut.

So a normal 1- or 2-pass part on a current Sodick cannot be posted as the control expects. Nothing gouges, and the workaround (`wire-iso`, or one operation per pass) exists, so P3 by the AGENTS.md table.

**Scope** (his suggestion): 2 passes first - entry `C000`, rough `C001`, sizing `C002`. Polishing (`C903+`) later.

**Open questions for the reporter** (asked on #617): where in the program each C word goes (on the threading/entry move, at each pass start); whether `C000` is used for every start hole; an example program from an LN control (his earlier AQ600L example on #617 shows a condition table in the header).

Clean-room: no CAM vendor's Sodick post or output is used; only the owner's own description and public Sodick manuals.

Done means: the Sodick post writes the C000/C001/C002 structure for a 1- and 2-pass Wire Contour, pinned by golden programs, and the owner confirms on an LN control (or the open questions are answered on this issue).

Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 1 of 5.

## Why
The ball drop-cutter of 3D finishing tests every facet for each sample. `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` lines 368-388) loops over all `Sup` entries with a padded box reject only. Each accepted candidate calls `ball_clear` (lines 132-142), which loops over all facets again. `column_clear` (line 162) does the same. There is no spatial index. The cost is about samples x facets.

The GPU filter of #2526 must match a CPU reference. This slice makes that reference: a CPU grid of facets that the GPU result is tested against. It is also the largest speed gain (estimate in #2526, comment 3/4).

## What
- Bin the `Sup` entries (from `build_sups`, lines 27-50) into a uniform XY grid by their padded box (`xmin..xmax`, `ymin..ymax`, already padded by `r`).

- The same f64 functions run. The subset must hold every facet whose padded box contains the query point. This keeps the result the same bits.
- Optional, same PR or a follow-up: run the raster lines in parallel with an order-preserving `collect`.
- No GPU code in this slice.

## Prime Directive
- The grid is conservative: a facet goes into each cell that its padded box touches. A bin miss would let `ball_clear` pass a ball that touches a facet. A test pins the superset rule.
- Degenerate input (NaN box, zero-area facet, a box past the coordinate guard) goes to every cell or gives a clean `GenError`. It never panics.

body:
Part of #2525 (slice 1 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What to add

Add a CPU module in `camcraft-geometry` (for example `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/`) that converts a `geo2d::Region` to a bit-packed grid of cells. This is the base of the raster nest of #2525. It has no GPU code and no wgpu.

- A grid has an origin, a cell size (integer, in `geo2d::SCALE` units) and a width and height in cells. Rows are packed in `u32` words.
- **Over-approximate mode** (for parts): mark each cell that the region touches. A cell that only touches the boundary is marked.
- **Under-approximate mode** (for the usable sheet): mark a cell free only when the full cell is inside the region. Holes of the region are not free.
- Use integer arithmetic on the `geo2d` integer coordinates only. No float enters the decision of a cell.
- Refuse by name: a non-positive cell size, a grid larger than a stated cell limit, a non-finite input, an empty region where one is required.
- One-line provenance comment: scanline polygon fill and conservative coverage, from Bennell and Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and general computer-graphics literature.

## Why

The raster finds nest positions fast. It is only a first filter. A raster "free" result must be a true "free" result: parts over-approximate, the sheet under-approximates (#2525, research comment 2).

## Notes

- No new crate edge, no new dependency, no decision entry for an edge. Record the cell-size default and the cell limit in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.
- No MCP tool: this is a kernel module with no command.
- Work that changes nest geometry is under the safety floor: `effort:high`.
- Headless tests only. No GPU.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/geometry/tests/` show:
- For squares, a part with a hole, a thin sliver and a rotated part, each point of the region lies in a marked cell (over-approximate), checked on a dense point sample.
- Each free cell of the under-approximate sheet lies fully inside the region (all four corners and the cell centre inside, and no region edge crosses the cell).
- The same input gives the same bits on each run.
- Each refusal names its reason.

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> when hitting simulation there sh ould be an option to "step" thru to next operation.. so we can check the one relevant

## Problem

The simulation plays the whole program from the first move. A user who wants to check one operation must scrub or wait. There is no way to go to the next operation.

## Wanted

1. The simulation controls have a "next operation" step. It moves the playback position to the first move of the next operation in program order.
2. A matching "previous operation" step. It moves to the start of the current operation, and a second press moves to the start of the one before it.
3. The control shows which operation is current (its name from the tree). A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change works the same as a step inside one setup.
4. The stock shown at the new position is correct: it is the stock after all earlier operations. A step must give the same stock as playback to that position. A step never skips a removal.
5. Disabled states: "next" is disabled in the last operation. "previous" is disabled at the start of the first operation. The AccessKit labels and the tooltips say what each button does.
6. A keyboard shortcut for each step, listed in the shortcut help.

## Notes

- The playback position is ephemeral UI state (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"), so no undoable command is needed. If a step selects an operation in the tree, that selection goes through `SelectEntity`.
- A skipped or suppressed operation is not a stop. An operation with no toolpath is not a stop.
- UI text: plain English, no G-code jargon. A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and the position, not pixel values (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`).
- Related: #2587 (the stand-alone simulator window). The same step logic should work there. Keep the operation-boundary lookup in the lowest crate that provides it, so both can use it.

## Done means

- A test shows that "next" from a position inside operation 1 gives the first move of operation 2, and that the stock equals the stock from plain playback to that move.
- Tests for the first operation, the last operation, a tool change and an operation with no toolpath.
- The behaviour tests and the page layout test of the simulation panel pass.

body:
Found during the quick gate of PR #2594 (#2340). The PR does not touch `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`.

## What happens

`diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` (`crates/ui/src/diag.rs:124`) fails in some full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`:

```
panicked at crates/ui/src/diag.rs:139:9:
the note is an INFO event: 2026-11-18T21:12:45.153099Z  WARN camcraft_ui: gpu: test adapter failed: no surface - trying the next adapter
```

The captured output has the WARN line, but not the INFO line ("headless: test adapter").

Readings on Linux, 12 cores, `--test-threads=10`, tree `v0.24.0` plus PR #2594:
- Full lib run: 1 failure in 3 runs (the quick gate step `ui suites: lib`; then two clean runs, 1170 passed).
- The test alone (`--exact`): 3 passes in 3 runs.

## Suspected cause (not confirmed)

- `diag::info` is one `tracing::info!` callsite. All UI code and all UI tests use it.
- The test installs its subscribers with `tracing::subscriber::with_default`, which is thread-local.
- `tracing` caches the interest of each callsite for the whole process. Other tests run on other threads at the same time, and a new dispatcher causes a rebuild of the cached interest.
- Thus the INFO callsite can be disabled while this test's "info" subscriber is the default on its thread. The WARN callsite stays enabled, which agrees with the output above.

## Expected

The test passes in each parallel run.

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Run the assertions in a separate process or a test binary of its own, so no other test shares the callsites.
- Call `tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache()` after the subscriber is installed, and before each event.
- Serialize the test with the other tests that emit `diag` lines (a lock, as `snapshot_guard` does for the theme cells in #2373).

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested by the precedent of #2373: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: `diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` passes in repeated full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, and the fix says which runs were measured.

## What a Tormach user has today

PathPilot can export and import its whole tool table as a `.csv` file (Tormach 770MX operator manual UM10587, section 7.6.4 "Import and Export the Tool Table"): **Offsets tab -> Export -> type a name -> save to a USB drive**; **Import** on the same tab loads a `.csv` back. CamCraft today:
- imports and exports tool libraries only as `.camtools` (`import_tool_library`, `export_tool_library`, #355, #899);
- writes a setup's tool list as a generic CSV for a spreadsheet (`tool_list_export.rs`, #389) - not PathPilot's column layout;
- has no docs page that tells a Tormach user how to get his machine's tools into CamCraft.

So a user re-types every tool (number, diameter, length, description) to make posted programs match the machine.

## What to do

1. **Docs** (site guide, Tormach section): how to export the PathPilot tool table (the steps above), how to bring it into CamCraft, and how the tool numbers map to `T<n>` in the posted program. Same page: the reverse, for PathPilot Hub tests.
2. **Import:** read a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` into the document's tools (or a `.camtools` library): tool number, diameter, length/offset, type and description where the file has them; the user completes what PathPilot does not store (flutes, flute length, holder). One undo step; an MCP tool (or a format option on `import_tool_library`); refuse by name a row it cannot read.
3. **Export (for Hub and the real machine):** write the document's tools as a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` that PathPilot's Import reads, so a Hub test or a real job starts with the same tool numbers and diameters as the posted program.

## Open point

The exact PathPilot CSV columns are not in the manual. mkinney will export his 770MX tool table; that file is the sample to build and pin the parser against (tests with a recorded `.csv`, no machine needed).

Done means: a docs page with the export/import steps; an import that reads the sample file into tools with the right numbers and diameters, pinned by a test; an export that PathPilot Hub imports (checked once in Hub).

title: Contour tabs: the bridge check compares only neighbouring cuts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The bridge check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs` came with PR #2486. It compares only two neighbouring cuts: the cut before a tab and the cut after it.

The check reads only the last `W + D` of the walk before the tab. It reads only the first `W + D` of the walk after the tab. Lead-in and lead-out moves are included.

A different cut can come closer than the tab width. The check does not read that cut. Two cases are known:

- A U-turn of the same ring. A later part of the ring comes near the tab.
- A different ring at the same level.

The reviewer of head `613ba4abf` says that the tab then holds through a strip that is narrower than W. Main had the same limit before PR #2486. The decision file `docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md` records this limit.

## Cases seen in the build review (not confirmed as tab necks)

- A 60 x 7 mm inside slot, W = 3 mm, 3 mm tabs. Two cut runs are 2.06 mm apart. The output has no note. The reviewer says the ring is almost a line here, so the distance is across the slot. The reviewer did not confirm a tab neck.
- An inside L-shape with Perpendicular, Arc or Tangential leads. Lead cuts on the two walls of a 14 mm arm come within 0.07 to 3.4 mm of each other. The cuts are in scrap material, far from the tabs. The reviewer says this was present before PR #2486 and is not a bridge failure.

## First step

Write a shape-mask test in `crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs` (see AGENTS.md, "2D toolpath shape-mask tests"). Use the U-turn case and the second-ring case. Measure the narrowest bridge.

- If no bridge is narrower than the tab width, post the result on this issue. Keep P3.
- If a bridge is narrower than the tab width, raise this issue to P1. AGENTS.md sets P1 for unsafe output.

## Smaller points

- [ ] `SLACK = 1e-6` (`tab_bridge.rs:77`) has no margin for arc chord error. The reviewer found no bridge under W in a probe, but says the margin is small.
- [ ] With a picked start, the windows grow backward only (`tab_bridge.rs:104`, `128-129`). If the first window grows past the pick, the first keep no longer starts at the pick. No note says this. `contour.rs:307-309` then checks `lead_held` on a keep that is not at the pick. The reviewer says this is not a gouge. Add a `tabs:` note, or a refusal by name.
- [ ] No test has more than one tabbed level. The tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs` use TAB_H = 1 and a stepdown of 2. The reviewer's probe with three levels gave a correct result. Add a test with more than one tabbed level.

## Done means

- The shape-mask result is posted on this issue.
- Each smaller point is fixed, or has a `tabs:` note or a named refusal, with a test that pins it.

Refs #2480
Found in the reviews of PR #2486.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15. His words: "Issue, on Geometry tabs, under Boundaries.. there should be selection for faces and edges that is "do not touch".. and he calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs."

## What is missing

An operation has no way to name model faces or edges that the tool must not touch. The user cannot protect a finished surface, a datum face or a sharp edge from a later operation.

## What to do

1. Add a "Do not touch" selection to the Boundaries group of the Geometry tab of an operation.
   - The user picks faces and edges in the viewport.
   - Each picked item shows as a row with a remove button.
   - The viewport shows the protected items in a different colour while the operation is selected.
2. Store the selection on the operation. The change goes through an undoable command (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"). The command ships with its MCP tool.
3. Add a clearance parameter (default 0, the stock to leave still applies). The tool stays this distance from each protected item.
4. Each generator that the operation type uses keeps the tool clear of the protected items. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges. The check uses the full tool: flutes, shank and holder.
5. The verify gate checks each generated move against the protected items. This check is independent of the generator.
6. If a move touches a protected item, the operation is refused or marked "incomplete" with a diagnostic that names the item. The post is blocked. The program is never posted with such a move (AGENTS.md "Prime Directive: Never Crash, Never Gouge").
7. If a protected item is also in the machining selection of the same operation, refuse the selection when the command is created. Say which item is in the two lists.
8. The project file stores the selection. Say in the PR if older builds refuse the new file.

## Scope

- First slice: the selection, the command, the MCP tool, the verify check and the refusal, for one 2D and one 3D operation type. The PR names the two types.
- Later slices: the other operation types. File one issue for each family (2D, 3D, multi-axis, turning, wire).
- Reference material is public machining literature and published user documentation at behaviour level only (AGENTS.md "Clean-Room Protocol"). Write the labels in our own words.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor. It adds a gouge law and can change posted G-code for an operation that has protected items. An operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before: pin that.

## Done means

- The Geometry tab has the "Do not touch" selection under Boundaries, with pick, list and remove.
- Undo and redo restore the selection. The MCP tool sets and reads it.
- A test with a protected face next to the cut region shows that no move comes nearer than the clearance.
- A test with a protected face that the selected region cannot avoid shows the refusal, with the item named, and a blocked post.
- A test shows that an operation without protected items gives a toolpath that does not change.
- The structural UI test asserts the new rows and their labels.
- The user guide describes the selection and the refusal.

body:
Standardize 3D `Deburr` on chamfer chord width `w`, add Constant Depth sizing, and support multi-pass edge breaks.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs` (`DeburrParams`)
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs` (`deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte`)
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `sane.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`
- `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` (`PROJECT_VERSION`), `crates/app/src/mcp/`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`

## What to change

1. Redefine `DeburrParams.width` and `OpParams::Deburr.width` as chamfer chord width `w = 2 * s * sin(theta / 2)` across all wedge angles `theta` (default `0.5 mm`). Keep `Chamfer2D.width` unchanged as its 2D horizontal leg width.
2. Increment `PROJECT_VERSION` (`61` -> `62`) and multiply legacy 3D `Deburr.width` values by `sqrt(2)` on load (the 90-degree corner ratio). Update `deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte` to pass `w = 2.0 * sqrt(2)`.
3. Add `break_mode` (`ConstantWidth` default, `ConstantDepth`), `break_profile` (`Chamfer` default, `Round`), and multi-pass step parameters to `DeburrParams` and `OpParams::Deburr`.
4. Compute setback `s = d / cos(theta / 2)` for `ConstantDepth`. Emit outer-to-final cone chamfer passes within `EdgeBreak::floor_at`, and refuse `Round` by name on sharp cones until ball-tipped cutters run.
5. Wire all settings through commands, project files, MCP `ParamsDto`, and UI controls.

## Done means

- Legacy v61 `Deburr` projects migrate cleanly by `sqrt(2)` and keep matching cut depth on 90-degree corners.
- `ConstantWidth` and `ConstantDepth` cones cut multi-pass bevels that stay inside `EdgeBreak` bounds and pass verify.
- `Round` on a sharp cone refuses by name, and UI, MCP, and migration tests pass.

Part of #1827

Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

The part is a 30 mm cube made of two L-shaped halves with 15 mm quadrant steps. Every edge, convex and concave, has an R3.125 mm fillet. The only cutter is a 1/4 in (6.35 mm) 3-flute **flat** end mill.

- **3D Finish takes only a ball nose** (`list_operation_types`: `"tool_kinds": ["BallNose"]`). With the flat end mill, the op is refused:
  `No ball-nose in Setup 2's tools - a 3D Finish operation cuts with one; add it ... 'BN-0600' (6 mm ball-nose)`
- There is no **z-level (waterline) finish** with a flat or bull-nose tool. That is the usual way to finish steep walls and convex fillets with the tool already in the spindle.
- The workaround was a **3D Pocket** with 0.15 mm (0.006 in) stepdowns used as "terraces" over the top fillets. That is a roughing strategy, so it leaves the 0.15 mm stair-steps the user has to accept. It also hit `feed moves ... cross in XY at shared depth` on the notch path.

## Expected

A finishing strategy that works with flat and bull-nose cutters:

- **z-level / waterline contours** on the model at a set stepdown (or scallop height), at least for steep regions;
- the tool's real shape (flat bottom, corner radius) used for the gouge offset;
- the shallow areas left to a later pass or flagged as rest.

A flat tool still cannot form a concave fillet smaller than its corner radius, and the rest check should say so. It can follow convex fillets and walls.

**Done means:** 3D Finish (or a new 3D Contour kind) accepts flat and bull-nose tools with a z-level pattern. On a filleted block with a flat end mill it generates gouge-free waterline passes at the set stepdown, and verify reports the concave-fillet rest. A pinning test covers the flat and bull-nose cases.

Launched by double-click (Explorer, Start menu, installer shortcut) there is no console and no redirect, so `camcraft_app::logging::init` writes the tracing log to a missing stderr handle and the log is lost. Only a start-up failure or panic is surfaced (message box, PR #1287).

Expected: with no console and no valid stderr, the log goes to a file in a per-user location (e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CamCraft\logs\camcraft-ui.log`, rotated or size-capped), and the start-up failure / panic message box names that path.

Notes: a terminal launch or a redirect must keep writing where it does today. Pick the location and rotation policy in a decision note; no new dependency without the maintainer's say (tracing-appender would be one).

Done means: a double-clicked `camcraft-ui.exe` on Windows writes its tracing log to a documented per-user file; the error message box names that file; terminal and redirected launches are unchanged; the pure part (path choice, "is stderr usable" decision) has a unit test.

Refs #1278

Part of #361.

**What happens.** A tool carries one body from one file. Modular tooling is sold and modelled in pieces: a clamping unit or basic holder on the turret or spindle, an adapter, a cutting head, the insert - joined at standardised interfaces (the issue names ISO 26622 and ISO 26623 polygon/taper couplings). Vendors publish one STEP per piece, so today the user must merge them in a CAD system before importing.

**Open design.** How a tool's body becomes a stack of placed pieces (each a file with its own placement relative to the one below), how the pieces mate (by the coordinate systems the files name, or by numbers), what the laws read (the union: one envelope for a spindle body, one set of clearance bands for a lathe body), and how it is saved. Only public documentation of the interface standards may be used; no vendor file is committed.

**Done means:** two synthetic pieces (our own STEPs) are attached to one tool, placed against each other, judged as one body, saved and reloaded; removing one piece is one undo step.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

body:
### What are you trying to do

A desired tool path type/output would be Peck Threading, where during the threading operation the tool will pull out of the cut a very tiny bit and then reengage to prevent long stringy chips in materials that are hard to form chips such as stainless steels and heat resistant super alloys.

### How you imagine it working

As part of the threading cycle (if supported by the controller) or as a raw point to point out put, the tool would move out of the cut by the depth of cut to break the chip. It should then do a spring pass at that depth to clean up the previous pass and get those couple of highspots to prevent a sudden spike in chip load on the pass at the next depth.
